reason: [V] evidence (40% earn under ₹15k, about ₹75/h net) suggests income is too low, not just uneven. A buffer you don't have to follow, and that thin surpluses can't fill, only shows the shortfall.
weakest_assumption: That good weeks leave enough spare money to fill a buffer, and that riders won't spend it under pressure.
missing_info: Real rider week-by-week income: how often lean months hit and how big the dips are.

fix.change: Test the rule on real or published income-volatility data and report the share of workers whose good weeks can actually fill a buffer.

reason: Lean weeks pushing me into loans is real [V]. But a buffer that's only a number on screen, with the cash still in my pocket, may not stop me spending it. Nothing shows riders would follow it.
weakest_assumption: Riders have leftover money in good weeks and will leave the buffer cash untouched under pressure.
missing_info: Real rider weekly income swings, and whether any rider sticks to a self-salary rule.

fix.change: Move good-week surplus automatically into the worker's own bank account, such as a recurring deposit set up by UPI autopay. The tool never holds the money. Also read earnings from a screenshot of the platform payout screen.

reason: The tool only gives advice and never holds money, so it avoids regulated payments and KYC. There is little room for fraud. The [V] evidence shows a real problem of borrowing in lean times.
weakest_assumption: That storing workers' income logs and Kannada voice notes needs no consent or data-protection controls.
missing_info: No consent flow, data retention policy, audit records or DPDP Act 2023 handling for personal income data.

fix.change: Add explicit consent capture, a time-stamped audit log of the rule's outputs, and a short data-retention and deletion policy in line with the DPDP Act.

reason: Shocks pushing workers into borrowing are verified, and the tool holding no money limits fraud loss. But a Kannada WhatsApp bot for low-literacy users is easy for scammers to impersonate.
weakest_assumption: Low-literacy users can tell the real WhatsApp bot apart from scammers copying it to steal UPI PINs.
missing_info: Who stores voice notes and income logs, and whether union or NGO staff can see them.

fix.change: Use one verified WhatsApp number that never asks for money, OTP, PIN or links. End every message with a spoken Kannada warning about this.

reason: A Kannada-only vendor with a keypad phone can't use WhatsApp. Kannada voice input is a plan, not built. Help from a union or NGO is only 'could'. She is left out.
weakest_assumption: That a basic or shared phone can send WhatsApp voice notes and receive warnings she can follow.
missing_info: A non-smartphone channel (IVR, missed call, SMS); who logs cash income for her; a Kannada voice test

fix.change: Add a Kannada IVR or missed-call line with spoken weekly self-salary amounts and warnings, plus a mode where an NGO helper enters income for her.

reason: The cash-flow pain is real [V], but the worker runs this alone. They log by hand every day, and the buffer is just a number they can ignore. Nothing covers missed logs.
weakest_assumption: Tired riders and vendors will log income by voice every day without fail.
missing_info: How many taps or voice notes per week, and what happens when logs are missed or misheard

fix.change: Make it one weekly voice note. Riders read out their platform payout total. If no note arrives, carry last week's figure forward and flag it.

reason: Verified distress borrowing makes the problem real. The core is a rule a person can check, holds no money, so worst-case harm is low. Risks are false warnings and income-data privacy.
weakest_assumption: Lean-month warnings fitted to synthetic data won't push riders into needless cuts to food or fuel.
missing_info: Where income logs and voice notes are stored, who can see them, and the consent flow.

fix.change: Show each warning as a range with its plain reasoning. Keep income data on the device or behind clear consent, and never share it with lenders or platforms.

reason: Problem is real [V], but the only prior-art evidence is unopened snippets [AI]. Nobody checked whether existing income-smoothing apps already serve Kannada-speaking riders, so what is actually new can't be judged.
weakest_assumption: That existing budgeting or gig-finance apps lack self-salary smoothing and Kannada voice input.
missing_info: A named check of existing income-smoothing apps and Indian gig-worker finance tools, and what they lack.

fix.change: Spend one hour opening 3-5 existing income-smoothing or gig-finance tools. Show in a side-by-side table that Kannada voice input for cash earners is the real gap.

reason: It answers F1 directly: a timing fix for uneven income, a labelled synthetic backtest for Evidence, and Kannada voice for the least-digital user. The tool never holds money, as the rule requires.
weakest_assumption: Synthetic income patterns are realistic enough that the backtest result means something for real riders.
missing_info: Real or published rider weekly income variance to calibrate the synthetic data

fix.change: Base synthetic income on published figures (IDInsight ₹75/h, seasonal and monsoon dips). Backtest difficult cases such as back-to-back lean weeks and an emergency withdrawal.

reason: Workers do borrow when income dips [V]. 'Pay yourself a fixed ₹X weekly' is a plain, teachable rule, and Kannada voice lowers the barrier. Nobody has tested whether users understand it.
weakest_assumption: Untrained users will grasp a buffer that's only a number on screen and stick to it.
missing_info: Any test of whether Kannada-speaking vendors or riders understand the warnings without a trainer.

fix.change: Send the weekly message as a short, plain Kannada voice note: 'Keep ₹X aside, spend ₹Y'. Test it with 3-5 real vendors or riders through an SHG or union.

reason: The core is a deterministic self-salary and buffer rule plus a backtest on labelled synthetic data. Four people can build and demo that in 21h. The problem is backed by [V] sources.
weakest_assumption: That Kannada voice and WhatsApp input will work reliably live, within 21h, with no real data.
missing_info: Which speech-to-text and WhatsApp APIs they will use, and whether access is already set up.

fix.change: Build the rule engine and backtest first. Keep a typed Kannada text fallback and pre-recorded voice clips, and treat live WhatsApp as a stretch goal.

reason: Distress borrowing is verified [V], but the premise that timing, not low income, is the cause has no source. Lean-month frequency and adherence are unknown; synthetic backtest is circular.
weakest_assumption: Riders' yearly income covers needs, so smoothing alone prevents shortfalls and debt.
missing_info: Real week-to-week rider income variance and size of dips; any evidence riders keep self-managed buffers.

fix.change: Base synthetic income on published rider earnings figures (IDInsight ₹75/h, seasonal dips), and show the rule fails when a good week leaves no surplus.
